latest_nl_proof:
Set I_i = (f_1,...,f_i) and R_i = S/I_i for 0 <= i <= d, with I_0 = (0) and R_0 = S. Because each f_j is homogeneous, each I_i is a homogeneous ideal, so each R_i is graded, and each graded piece (R_i)_m is a quotient of S_m.

First compute Hilb_S(q). A monomial x_1^{a_1}...x_d^{a_d} has degree a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d. For fixed m there are only finitely many tuples (a_1,...,a_d) in N^d with that weighted sum, because each a_j <= m/w_j and each w_j > 0. Thus the monomials of weighted degree m form a finite basis of S_m, so
Hilb_S(q) = sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q S_m) q^m = sum_{(a_1,...,a_d) in N^d} q^{a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d}.
Since this is a finite product of geometric series in Q[[q]],
Hilb_S(q) = product_{j=1}^d (sum_{r >= 0} q^{r w_j}) = product_{j=1}^d 1/(1 - q^{w_j}).
When d = 0 this is the empty product 1, i.e. Hilb_Q(q) = 1.

Now fix i with 1 <= i <= d, and write again f_i for its image in R_{i-1} = S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}). By assumption, this image is not a zero-divisor. Since f_i is homogeneous of degree e_i, multiplication by f_i sends (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i} to (R_{i-1})_m for each m >= 0; here we interpret (R_{i-1})_t = 0 for t < 0. Thus for each m there is a linear map
mu_{i,m} : (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i} -> (R_{i-1})_m,  u |-> f_i u.
It is injective because f_i is not a zero-divisor in R_{i-1}.

Let pi_{i,m} : (R_{i-1})_m -> (R_i)_m be the natural quotient map, where R_i = R_{i-1}/(f_i) = S/(f_1,...,f_i). This map is surjective. Its kernel is exactly f_i (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i}. Indeed, since R_i = R_{i-1}/(f_i), an element of (R_{i-1})_m lies in ker(pi_{i,m}) exactly when it lies in the ideal f_i R_{i-1}. If v in (R_{i-1})_m and v = f_i u for some u in R_{i-1}, write u as a finite sum of homogeneous components: u = sum_t u_t with u_t in (R_{i-1})_t. Then
v = sum_t f_i u_t,
and each summand f_i u_t is homogeneous of degree t + e_i. Because the grading is a direct sum decomposition and v itself is homogeneous of degree m, all components of degrees different from m must vanish. Hence v = f_i u_{m-e_i}. So ker(pi_{i,m}) = im(mu_{i,m}).

Therefore, for every m >= 0, we have a short exact sequence
0 -> (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i} -> (R_{i-1})_m -> (R_i)_m -> 0.
Taking dimensions over Q gives
(dim_Q (R_i)_m) = (dim_Q (R_{i-1})_m) - (dim_Q (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i}).

Now sum over m >= 0:
Hilb_{R_i}(q)
= sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q (R_i)_m) q^m
= sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q (R_{i-1})_m) q^m - sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q (R_{i-1})_{m-e_i}) q^m
= Hilb_{R_{i-1}}(q) - q^{e_i} Hilb_{R_{i-1}}(q)
= (1 - q^{e_i}) Hilb_{R_{i-1}}(q).
The reindexing in the second sum is valid because the pieces of negative degree are 0.

Applying this successively for i = 1,2,...,d, we obtain
Hilb_{R_d}(q) = product_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i}) Hilb_{R_0}(q) = product_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i}) Hilb_S(q).
Since R_d = S/(f_1,...,f_d), substituting the formula for Hilb_S(q) gives
Hilb_{S/(f_1,...,f_d)}(q)
= product_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i}) * product_{i=1}^d 1/(1 - q^{w_i})
= product_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i})/(1 - q^{w_i})
in Q[[q]].

This is exactly the required identity, and when d = 0 both sides are 1 by the empty-product convention.
role_in_parent: Turns the regular-sequence realization from L4 into the exact rational product that equals the q-binomial quotient.
statement_nl: Let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1, ..., w_d and e_1, ..., e_d be positive integers, and let S := Q[x_1, ..., x_d] be graded by deg(x_i) = w_i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Let f_1, ..., f_d be homogeneous elements of S with deg(f_i) = e_i, and assume that for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. For a graded Q-vector space M = direct sum_{m >= 0} M_m with each M_m finite-dimensional, define Hilb_M(q) := sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q M_m) q^m. Then Hilb_{S/(f_1, ..., f_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / (1 - q^(w_i)) as an identity in Q[[q]], with the empty product equal to 1 if d = 0.

domain_restrictions: If d=0, then S is interpreted as Q and the empty product equals 1
For i=1,...,d: w_i and e_i are positive integers (so no weight/degree is 0 or negative)
S is a graded polynomial ring with weights: deg(x_i)=w_i and induced grading on S
Each f_i is homogeneous and has graded degree exactly e_i
For each i, f_i modulo (f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is a non-zero-divisor in the quotient ring S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1})
Hilbert series is defined for graded Q-vector spaces M=⊕_{m≥0} M_m with each M_m finite-dimensional
The stated identity is in the ring of formal power series Q[[q]]
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim:
Given weighted grading deg(x_i)=w_i on S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0), and homogeneous elements f_i
together with deg(f_i)=e_i (w_i,e_i>0) such that for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is a non-zero-divisor, then the Hilbert series of the graded quotient M:=S/(f_1,...,f_d) satisfies, as an identity of formal power series in Q[[q]],
Hilb_{S/(f_1,...,f_d)}(q)=\prod_{i=1}^d \frac{1-q^{e_i}}{1-q^{w_i}}, with the convention that if d=0 the product is 1.
quantifier_order: Define S := Q[x_1,...,x_d] graded by deg(x_i)=w_i (or S:=Q if d=0)
∀ (f_i)_{1≤i≤d} with f_i ∈ S homogeneous and deg(f_i)=e_i
Assumption: for each i=1,...,d, the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor
Then equality holds for M := S/(f_1,...,f_d) as an identity in Q[[q]]
